affirmativeChain: Article1 plants expressly includes live or dead plants/parts (English PDFp2; original Arabicp2).
Article1 agricultural consignment separately includes plants (same pages); Article1 importer includes natural persons/consignees (Englishp4;Arabicp3).

Article3 covers cases specified by the Law and executive regulations (Englishp6;Arabicp4); Article5(2) is a direct all-imported-consignment certificate duty (Englishp8;Arabicp6), not only a later designated list.
Physical rolled/dried sencha leaf parts are conservatively included; documentary duty therefore prevents the no-certificate route.

analysis.actualCategory: The product remains identifiable physical tea leaves after steaming, rolling, hot-air drying and finishing. Article1 expressly covers dead plants/parts; the Arabic original confirms that wording. This is a stronger textual dead-material inclusion than TC's plant-parts definition without a living qualification. It does not mean every chemically derived plant ingredient is necessarily a plant part.
analysis.affirmativeDuty: Article1 agricultural consignment includes plants, plant products, or other regulated materials. Article5(2) then imposes certification on every imported/transit agricultural consignment. The final qualification concerning other regulated materials does not textually convert the separately enumerated plants limb into a future-designated-only category. Article3 limits application to cases specified by the Law and its executive regulations; Article5 is itself such an operative case. Article1's reference to a single certificate where appropriate describes consignment documentation and does not cancel the express all-consignment duty.
analysis.strongestContrary: Article1 definitions apply unless context requires otherwise. The more specific manufactured-product limb regulates manufactured materials only when their nature/processing can introduce/spread pests. MAFF-described sencha manufacture plus ISPM32 Category1 tea is strong factual evidence of sufficient processing. Reading finished tea exclusively in that product limb avoids overlapping definitions and fits Article2 pest-prevention purpose and Article4(1)(i)/(o) standards-related duties. This is a plausible favorable reading, not dismissed simply because tea is unnamed. It nevertheless requires the independent explicit dead-plant-part limb to yield; no provision in the full Act states that allocation. The conservative proposal retains the express dead-parts wording rather than claiming technical pest risk proved.
analysis.designationCheck: Article4 gives regulatory powers and Article14 permits further prohibitions/restrictions. Those powers are not the source of the proposed certificate duty; Article5(2) already supplies it directly for the defined consignment. Do not infer duty from mere enabling powers or customs tax-table absence.
analysis.exceptions: Article5(5)(c) is an administrative power to cancel prescribed conditions based on risk within the listed Ministry measures; it does not state a self-executing manufactured-food exemption. Article27(2) preserves older regulations only so far as compatible. The saved JKI partial German translation of Decision248/2003 Article2 uses living plants, but cannot narrow the newer Act's express live/dead definition. Its Article15(5) personal exception concerns traveler permits and Article25 small-quantity certificate exception concerns carried fruit/cut flowers/bulbs/tubers; neither establishes an automatic Japan postal-tea waiver. That partial translation is supplementary, not proof of absence of every possible older rule.
analysis.japanGuidance: Fresh original MAFF PDF page1 is dated21April2026 and has UAE Q*11 in the manufactured-green-tea column. Q means export with phytosanitary certificate; *11 warns some items may fall outside quarantine with neither permit nor certificate. JETRO August2025 separately states processed dried tea/matcha may be exempt subject to UAE confirmation; it predates the new Act. These are qualified corroboration, not an unconditional national duty or waiver.
analysis.privateFood: Existing personal-food registration exemption and unaccompanied-personal-food guidance are preserved. Their quantity/category gaps are not used as an independent certificate barrier. No commercial food documentation list is imported into private-post scope.
analysis.confidence: Moderate legal-scope inference supporting conservative operational exclusion; not a definitive tea-specific administrative determination.
analysis.comparisonWithTC: Both laws have an independent broad plant-parts limb and an affirmative document duty, despite a separate manufactured-product risk limb. AE additionally says dead expressly. TC uses prior permit sections34–35; AE uses Article5(2) certificate. This supplies a substantive consistent distinction from BH/MV/KN/VC living-plant-plus-risk-manufacture regimes.

freshAccessLimits: UAE legislation portal returned403; complete authoritative copies already recovered and read. No repeated commodity lookup failures or new generic searches used.
notConclusion: No claim of categorical tea prohibition, no proven botanical pest risk, no claim every processed plant ingredient is a plant part, and no automatic legal effect attributed to ISPM32.

independentPeerReview.assessment: Independently read current AE law previously; no further operative condition identified that defeats Article1 dead-part / consignment plus Article5(2) certificate chain. Contextual overlap and MAFF/JETRO possible exemptions are material contrary evidence, not a recovered controlling domestic waiver. Agrees moderate expressly conservative certificate-required leaf-part inference is defensible if applied consistently; no general permit conclusion.
